LESSON: CLASSES OF FIRE.

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds
Topic 1.3: Classes of fire.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Classes of fire., part of Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: What are the dangers of fire in nature? 2. How do effective fire control methods contribute to environmental preservation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign words related to fire for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Classes of fire. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify causes of fire in nature,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Classes of fire. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain the role of the fire triangle in the spread of fire,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Classes of fire. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. describe ways of controlling fires in nature,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Classes of fire. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. acknowledge the dangers of fires in nature. ● In groups, learners are guided to search for the meaning and sign of the words related to fire from digital and print media. Ensure that learners observe proper cyber ethics while conducting online searches. ● in pairs, learners practise fingerspelling and signing the words related to fire. In the absence of conventional signs, learners are guided to create and harmonise meaningful signs for communication purposes. ● in groups, learners are guided to discuss the possible causes of fire in 1. Ensure proper a proper seating arrangement that allows learners to have a face -to - face conversation. ● in groups, learners are guided to use print and digital media to search for the roles of the fire triangle in the spread of fire. ● in groups, learners are guided to discuss the role of the fire triangle in the spread of fire. Learners to be seated in an appropriate arrangement that supports the use of bilingual communication. ● in pairs, learners brainstorm on the different classes of fire and make summary notes. Ensure that learners who are hard of hearing are paired with those who are 12 deaf to enhance total communication and lip - reading. ● in groups, learners are guided to engage a resource person on the role of the fire triangle in the spread of fire. ● in groups, learners are guided to discuss the dangers of fires in the environment. ● in pairs, learners are guided to practise fire control measures. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

B. At home with your parent or guardian

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner acquires teamwork skills as the learners prepare posters on classes of fires

and their control measures in groups.

● Citizenship: Learner develops active community life skills while making posters on classes of fires and their control

14

measures and hanging at school, home and neighbouring markets.

Values:
● Respect: The learner appreciates diverse opinions during group discussion to classify fire according to the cause and suggest

control measures.

● Responsibility: The learner observes safety precautions when dealing with fires and flammable materials while practicing

fire control measures with peers.

Link to other subjects

The learner can relate the firefighting techniques used in Pre -Technical Studies as some of the ways of controlling fire in nature.
